input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated coroutine write into the same dict.
- rationale: Trigger: two asyncio tasks await the same decorated async function at the same time. Mechanism: the second call's stats.clear() wipes the dict the first call is updating, and both copies write to that single dict. Previously each call got a fresh dict, so the calls were isolated. Impact: statistics read through wrapped.statistics for either in-flight call show values belonging to the other call, or reset values.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is cleared and reused, so concurrent calls collide when the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's data. It only covers the async case, but that case is explicitly part of the label's failure path.
